nodes.description: Normal synovial joint formation requires interzone specification, suppression of chondrogenesis across the future joint line, and cavitation. Excessive BMP signaling (SYNS1, SYNS2, gain-of-function SYNS4), reduced interzone FGF9 signaling (SYNS3), and 3' regulatory reduction of GDF6 dosage (SYNS4) replace prospective synovial joint spaces with continuous mineralized cartilage and bone, producing congenital or postnatally progressive synostoses across limb, spinal, and stapedovestibular joints.

nodes.description: SYNS3 is caused by heterozygous missense substitutions in FGF9 (such as p.S99N and dimer-interface variants such as p.W144R) that disrupt FGF9-FGFR-heparin interaction or dimer-interface stability and reduce FGFR/ERK signaling in developing joints, cranial sutures, and palatal mesenchyme. Wild-type FGF9 normally restrains mesenchymal cells from premature chondrogenic differentiation by downregulating Sox6 and Sox9 while sustaining Gdf5 expression in the prospective joint interzone; altered FGF9 signaling disrupts interzone formation while also predisposing a subset of SYNS3 individuals to premature cranial suture fusion and cleft palate.
